objective.value: Experimentally evaluate 40 computationally predicted candidate transcription factors in Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 using multiplexed ChIP-exo to determine which are genuine DNA-binding TFs, map their genome-wide binding sites, compare their locations with RNAP/RpoD binding, classify them by target-gene count (global/local/single-target), and infer and validate the physiological functions of representative TFs via RNA-seq and deletion-mutant phenotyping.
objective.extraction_method: direct reading of abstract, introduction, results and Figure 1 caption
objective.notes: Study is the second application of a prediction-then-ChIP validation pipeline previously published by the same group (ref 10); the candidate list itself was generated previously.

hypothesis.value: A rank-ordered list of uncharacterized 'y-gene' proteins predicted by the TFpredict algorithm includes genuine transcription factors; multiplexed ChIP-exo combined with RNAP/sigma70 ChIP-exo and RNA-seq of knockout mutants can validate these TFs in vivo and reveal their regulatory and physiological roles, bringing the count of validated E. coli K-12 MG1655 TFs close to the estimated total of ~280.
hypothesis.extraction_method: synthesis of explicitly stated aims and rationale in abstract/introduction/results
hypothesis.notes: Specific per-TF hypotheses (e.g., ygbI mutation conferring growth benefit on tartrate, ref 44) are recorded in the corresponding experiment objects.

strain.value: Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 (parental/wild type) and its derivatives: 40 C-terminally 8-myc-tagged strains (one per candidate TF) generated by lambda red-mediated site-specific recombination, and single-gene deletion strains used for functional validation (explicitly tested: ΔyfeC, ΔyciT, ΔybcM, ΔygbI; ΔyidZ used for RNA-seq). Full strain list in Dataset S1 (not available in parsed text).
strain.extraction_method: direct reading of Methods (bacterial strains), Results, figure captions and Table 2
strain.notes: Exact genotypes of deletion strains are only in Dataset S1 (supplement-dependent). paper_label 'wild type' denotes unmodified MG1655, which is itself a standard lab strain, not a natural isolate.

genotype.value: Per-strain genotypes: MG1655 with chromosomal C-terminal 8-myc fusion at each of the 40 candidate TF loci; single-gene deletions ΔyidZ, ΔyfeC, ΔyciT, ΔybcM, ΔygbI (each separate; no combined genotypes shown). Deletion method and resistance markers not stated in the main text (Dataset S1).
genotype.extraction_method: direct reading of Methods and Results; supplement-dependent details flagged
genotype.notes: Deletions were constructed and tested separately; no combinatorial mutants reported. Tag insertion described as targeting the C-terminal region via lambda red recombination (ref 12 method).

engineering_method.value: Lambda red-mediated site-specific recombination to fuse an 8-myc epitope tag at the C-terminus of each candidate TF at its native chromosomal locus (method per Cho et al. 2006, ref 12); single-gene deletion mutants for phenotypic validation (construction method not described in main text). These are enabling modifications for a discovery/characterization study, not production-oriented engineering.
engineering_method.notes: Deletion strain construction protocol is supplement/as-described-previously dependent; main text does not specify.

value: Group A: 40 myc-tagged strains, each subjected to multiplexed ChIP-exo (barcoded first adapters, pooled library) to map TF binding sites; most under standard glucose M9 conditions; YbcM additionally under paraquat-induced oxidative stress.
Group B: MG1655 wild type subjected to ChIP-exo with anti-RNAP beta' (NT63) and anti-sigma70 (2G10) antibodies to map RNAP and RpoD binding.
Group C: paired RNA-seq comparisons, wild type vs individual TF deletion strains (ΔyidZ, ΔyfeC, ΔyciT, ΔygbI explicitly; five additional TFs in supplement).
Group D: phenotype assays - ΔyciT vs WT growth on M9 with glucose/fructose/sorbitol and M9 sorbitol ± 0.5 M NaCl; ΔybcM vs WT survival after 60 mM H2O2; ΔygbI vs WT growth on 20 mM L-tartrate.
Group E: in silico analyses only - SUPERFAMILY/HMM family annotation, SWISS-MODEL homology models, MEME motif search, COG enrichment.

value: 34 of 40 candidate TFs confirmed as DNA-binding proteins in vivo; 588 total binding sites identified; six candidates (YgeR, YggD, YjjJ, YfjR, YeeY, YpdC) showed no binding under tested conditions.
283/588 (48%) TF binding events overlap RNAP binding (208 RNAP+RpoD type, 75 RNAP-only type).
Classification: 1 global regulator (YidZ, 118 sites), 29 local regulators, 4 single-target regulators; consensus motifs obtained for 7 TFs (palindromic for YciT, YcjW, YdcN, YidZ).
Total validated E. coli K-12 MG1655 TF count expanded to 276 (authors report ~12% increase), close to the estimated ~280-300 total.

ΔyidZ: 74 genes differentially expressed (19 of 118 direct targets), including down-regulation of acid-stress/amino-acid genes (gadA, gadBC, hdeD, hdeAByhiD) and up-regulation of carbohydrate genes (rbsD, malM, malE, malX); no significantly enriched COG.

ΔyfeC: 124 up- and 81 down-regulated genes; 20/50 binding-site genes differentially expressed, 16/20 repressed; functions span transport/metabolism, translation, post-translational modification, cell envelope (lpp).

ΔyciT: target genes ybiV, ybiY, fsaA, cusF differentially expressed; no major growth defect on glucose/fructose/sorbitol (slightly lower stationary OD600); impaired growth under 0.5 M NaCl osmotic stress on sorbitol -> YciT involved in osmolarity control.

ΔybcM: 12 binding sites (11/12 upstream), autoregulation at ybcLM, targets include ucpA and ubiT-yhbS/ubiUV region; WT survival 8-fold higher than ΔybcM after 60 mM H2O2 15 min -> YbcM involved in ROS stress response.

ΔygbI: single divergent binding site overlapping ygbJ promoter; ygbJKLMN cluster upregulated upon deletion; ΔygbI (but not WT) grows on 20 mM L-tartrate -> YgbI is a repressor of the L-tartrate catabolic pathway.
Data deposited: GEO GSE159777 (ChIP-exo) and GSE159658 (RNA-seq).
outcomes.extraction_method: direct reading of Results, Discussion and figure captions
outcomes.notes: Proposed TF physiological roles are author inferences from binding + expression + phenotype data; mechanistic claims (e.g., YgbI blocking RNAP) supported by binding overlap but not by direct biochemical competition assays.

experimental_design_object.paper_scope_note: This is a discovery/characterization study (TRN expansion), not a production-oriented engineering study. Per the Q1/Q2/Q3 filter in section 5.5, none of the experiments constitute engineering decisions aimed at a production or phenotype-engineering goal: the myc-tagging and gene deletions are enabling/perturbation tools for characterization, so they fail Q1 as defined (they are not metabolic/biosensor/evolutionary/protein/chassis engineering actions toward a product or performance objective) and fail Q3 (no future design choice is altered). Accordingly, ddr_annotation objects are not attached; per-experiment decision_type labels are provided instead, and no generalizable_rule fields are fabricated.

experiments.purpose: Identify in vivo genome-wide binding sites of 40 computationally predicted candidate TFs to determine which are genuine DNA-binding proteins
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fails: no engineering action toward a production/phenotype goal; the experiment measures DNA binding of candidate proteins to validate computational predictions.
experiments.host: E. coli K-12 MG1655 derivative strains, each carrying a chromosomal C-terminal 8-myc tag on one candidate TF (40 strains; Dataset S1)
experiments.intervention: Lambda red-mediated C-terminal 8-myc tagging (construction; per strain); multiplexed ChIP-exo with anti-myc 9E10 antibody; barcoded first adapters pooled for library prep; most strains in glucose M9 at OD600 0.5; YbcM profiled additionally under 250 uM paraquat oxidative stress (20 min from OD600 0.3)
experiments.conditions: M9 minimal + 0.2% glucose, 37 degC, mid-log (OD600 ~0.5); 1% formaldehyde 25 min RT cross-linking; 2.5 M glycine 5 min quench; per-strain conditions listed in Dataset S2 (supplement-dependent)
experiments.control: Mock IP as S/N denominator in peak calling (S/N >= 1.5 filter); no untagged-strain IP control described in main text
experiments.readout: ChIP-exo sequencing on HiSeq 2500; bowtie mapping to NC_000913.2; MACE peak calling with S/N and bimodal-shape filters
experiments.analysis: Peak-to-gene assignment by genomic position; binding sites classified intragenic vs regulatory; MetaScope/SignalMap visualization
experiments.outcome: 34/40 candidates show DNA binding; 588 total binding sites; YgeR/YggD/YjjJ/YfjR/YeeY/YpdC show no binding under tested conditions

experiments.purpose: Map RNAP (beta') and sigma70 (RpoD) binding to determine the relative position of TF binding sites to the transcription machinery
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fails: measurement/characterization of RNAP and RpoD binding landscapes; no engineering intervention.
experiments.host: E. coli K-12 MG1655 wild type
experiments.intervention: ChIP-exo with NT63 (anti-RNAP beta') and 2G10 (anti-sigma70) antibodies
experiments.conditions: same ChIP-exo workflow and growth conditions as EXP1
experiments.readout: ChIP-exo binding maps for RNAP and RpoD
experiments.analysis: Classification of TF binding events into (i) RNAP+RpoD, (ii) RNAP only, (iii) others
experiments.outcome: 208 type-(i) and 75 type-(ii) events; 283/588 (48%) TF binding sites overlap RNAP

experiments.purpose: Determine consensus binding motifs of validated TFs
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fails: pure sequence analysis of measured binding regions.
experiments.host: in silico on binding-region sequences from reference genome NC_000913.2
experiments.analysis: Consensus motifs for 7 TFs (YciT, YcjW, YdcN, YdhB, YfeC, YfeD, YidZ); palindromic motifs for YciT, YcjW, YdcN, YidZ
experiments.outcome: 7 consensus motifs obtained; 8 additional TFs show sequence-specific patterns despite few sites

experiments.purpose: Identify genes directly regulated by each representative TF by comparing WT and TF-deletion transcriptomes
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fails: gene deletions here are perturbations to measure regulatory function, not engineering actions toward a product or performance objective; no subsequent design choice is driven (Q3 fails).
experiments.host: E. coli K-12 MG1655 WT and single-gene deletion strains (ΔyidZ, ΔyfeC, ΔyciT, ΔygbI in main text; others in supplement)
experiments.intervention: single-gene deletion (construction method not specified in main text; strains listed in Dataset S1)
experiments.conditions: same growth conditions as ChIP-exo experiments; mid-log harvest; RNAprotect stabilization
experiments.control: WT MG1655 grown and processed in parallel
experiments.readout: strand-specific paired-end RNA-seq (KAPA Hyper Prep, HiSeq 2500); bowtie v1.2.3 + summarizeOverlaps + DESeq2 (TPM; Wald test; BH adjustment; |log2FC| >= 1 and padj < 0.05)
experiments.analysis: DEG sets intersected with ChIP-exo binding targets to define direct regulons
experiments.outcome: ΔyidZ: 74 DEGs (19/118 direct); ΔyfeC: 124 up/81 down, 20 direct regulon genes (16 repressed); ΔyciT: ybiV/ybiY/fsaA/cusF differentially expressed; ΔygbI: 113 DEGs including upregulated ygbJKLMN

experiments.purpose: Test physiological role of YciT in carbon-source utilization and osmotic stress
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1/Q3 fail: phenotype verification of an already-constructed deletion strain under panel conditions; no engineering action and no future design choice altered.
experiments.host: E. coli K-12 MG1655 WT and ΔyciT
experiments.intervention: ΔyciT deletion strain (pre-existing within study) exposed to alternative carbon sources and osmotic stress
experiments.conditions: M9 minimal + 0.2% (w/v) glucose, fructose, or sorbitol; osmotic variant: M9 sorbitol + 0.5 M NaCl at culture start; 37 degC with agitation; 1/200 dilution from overnight; OD600 every 30 min

experiments.readout: growth curves on Bioscreen C; Figure 5D shows SD bands

experiments.purpose: Confirm YbcM role in oxidative stress response by comparing WT and ΔybcM survival under H2O2
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1/Q3 fail: survival measurement of pre-existing deletion strain; validates prediction, drives no new design.

experiments.intervention: ΔybcM deletion strain challenged with H2O2

experiments.control: WT MG1655 treated identically; untreated cells at time zero as survival baseline (percent survival)

experiments.readout: viable counts; percent survival relative to t=0

experiments.purpose: Verify YgbI function as repressor of the L-tartrate catabolic pathway via growth profiling of WT vs ΔygbI on L-tartrate
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1/Q3 fail: growth verification of pre-existing deletion strain; hypothesis originated from prior literature (ref 44), and the test does not change future design choices within this paper.

experiments.intervention: ΔygbI deletion strain grown on L-tartrate

experiments.control: WT MG1655 in the same medium

experiments.outcome: ΔygbI grows on L-tartrate whereas WT does not; supports model of YgbI directly repressing ygbJK promoter and indirectly inhibiting ygbLM/ygbN

experiments.purpose: Annotate TF family types and oligomeric states of candidate TFs to contextualize binding behavior
experiments.readout: SUPERFAMILY 2 HMM annotation; SWISS-MODEL homology models; VMD visualization; UniProt annotation

reusable_design_patterns: Prediction-to-validation pipeline: homology-based TF candidate ranking (TFpredict) -> chromosomal epitope tagging (lambda red, C-terminal 8-myc) -> multiplexed barcoded ChIP-exo for parallel binding mapping of 40 proteins in pooled libraries.
Reference-layer integration: RNAP (beta') and sigma70 ChIP-exo maps used to classify TF binding events by promoter context (RNAP+RpoD / RNAP-only / others) for coarse functional assignment.

Triangulation for direct regulons: ChIP-exo binding + RNA-seq of TF deletion (|log2FC| >= 1, padj < 0.05) + motif enrichment (MEME) to separate direct from indirect targets (e.g., 20/50 for YfeC, 19/118 for YidZ).
Target-number-based TF classification (global >100, local <100, single-target) to prioritize representative TFs for deep phenotyping.

Condition-matched phenotyping: hypothesis-driven selection of stress/carbon conditions per TF (paraquat ChIP for YbcM; NaCl osmotic growth for YciT; L-tartrate growth for YgbI) rather than a uniform phenotype screen.
Growth-defect readout with Bioscreen C (OD600 every 30 min, 3 biological replicates x 2 repetitions) and CFU-based survival under lethal H2O2 with percent-survival normalization to t=0.
